findings.summary: Two hashtags name programming languages that this language-agnostic GraphQL operations part never covers.
findings.evidence: "#javascript","#typescript" alongside caption topics "cost limits and alias-bombing, GraphQL vs REST, cursor connections, when not to use GraphQL, and a cheat sheet for production operations"
findings.fix: Replace "#javascript" and "#typescript" with topic-relevant tags such as "#restapi" and "#apisecurity".

findings.summary: The Cost Limits bullets give the reason for cost limits last, after the mechanisms it explains.
findings.evidence: Bullets order: "Score each field, multiply by list-size arguments" → "Reject over budget BEFORE anything executes" → "`maxDepth: 10` stops ..." → "Flexibility means the server cannot predict its workload"
findings.fix: Move "Flexibility means the server cannot predict its workload" to the top of the Cost Limits bullets, so the problem comes before the scoring and depth-limit fixes.

findings.summary: The page says offset paging "drifts" but never shows or explains how, so the reader can't see why cursors are more stable.
findings.evidence: "Offset paging drifts; cursors are the stable default"
findings.fix: Add a short example: "An insert while you page with skip: 10 shifts every row down, so page 2 repeats an item; a cursor keeps its place."

findings.summary: The Connections code uses `after: $cur` and `endCursor` without saying that the endCursor from one page becomes the next request's `after` value.
findings.fix: Add one line under the code: "Pass pageInfo.endCursor back as $cur to fetch the next page; stop when hasNextPage is false."
